summary.name: The Production Readiness Spectrum
summary.one_liner: A 2020 blog article explaining how to introduce Production Readiness Reviews (PRRs), checklists, and review and evaluation methods to an organization.
use_cases: Deciding whether a service is ready for production
Introducing a production readiness review process in an organization
Choosing a review method for service launches
Assessing on-call readiness of existing services
summary.what_it_does: The article defines production readiness as a spectrum that changes over time, and links it to SLIs and SLOs. It explains how Production Readiness Reviews document operational practices and use a checklist covering areas such as architecture, development process, change management, capacity planning, observability, and incident response. It describes four review styles (1-sided, group, semi-automated, automated) and several evaluation approaches (licking-the-index-finger, short-circuit, traffic-lights, score-based). It also covers how to propose the process, run trials, and keep the checklist current.
notable: Covers four review styles from manual 1-sided reviews to fully automated scorecards, with LinkedIn cited as an automated example
Presents traffic-lights (critical/important/suggested) and score-based evaluation models for launch decisions
Cites Atul Gawande's The Checklist Manifesto on ignorance versus ineptitude
caveats: Describes an approach and process rather than a software tool; it is an article, not a product
Automated reviews require upfront investment and ongoing maintenance, per the article
